question_text: The employer, not the salesman and the representative, _______ responsible for the loss.
explanation: The subject is 'The employer' (singular). The phrase 'not the salesman and the representative' is parenthetical and does not change the verb to plural.

question_text: The benefit one gets from watching plays _______ comparable to that found in taking a University degree in drama.
explanation: The subject is 'The benefit' (singular), so the verb must be singular ('is').

question_text: If Remi performs poorly in her forthcoming examination, then either her mother or I _______ to blame.
explanation: In an 'either/or' construction, the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. 'I' takes 'am'.

question_text: I am not attending _______ my wife.
explanation: 'Either' is used to present a choice between two alternatives.

question_text: _______ several bad air crashes recently.
explanation: 'There have been' is the present perfect plural form that agrees with 'several bad air crashes'.

question_text: _______ the main points of the lecture given by the Director of the Institute.
explanation: 'Those were' is plural and agrees with the plural noun 'points'.

question_text: The present wanton display of riches _______ morals in our society.
explanation: The subject is 'display' (singular), so the verb is 'is affecting'.

question_text: Each of the contestants _______ a chance to win.
explanation: 'Each' is a singular indefinite pronoun, so it takes a singular verb 'has'.

question_text: The only set of loud speakers available _______ to be connected according to the instruction.
explanation: The subject is 'The only set' (singular), so the verb is 'is'.

question_text: Many a candidate _______ to realise the difference between written and spoken English.
explanation: 'Many a' is followed by a singular noun and a singular verb ('fails').

question_text: All _______ well with Peter at the moment.
explanation: 'All' referring to a state of affairs is singular, so it takes 'is'.

question_text: One of the ladies who _______ in the premises _______ been asked to withdraw.
explanation: The subject is 'One' (singular) for the main verb 'has'. However, the relative pronoun 'who' refers to 'ladies' (plural), so it takes 'sell'.

question_text: A Tale of Two Cities, _______ we are studying for the examination.
explanation: The title of a book is treated as singular ('is'). 'Novel' is the singular noun.

question_text: We must not take us with the feelings of inadequacy _______ experienced during our preparations for the debate.
explanation: The relative pronoun 'that' refers to the singular 'feelings of inadequacy' as a concept, taking 'was'.

question_text: In my opinion, neither the players nor the coach _______ praise for the result of the match.
explanation: In a 'neither/nor' construction, the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. 'The coach' is singular, so 'deserves' is correct.

question_text: Knowledge of figures of speech as well as of idioms and lexical items _______.
option_a: in this section, A is tested
explanation: The subject is 'Knowledge' (singular). The phrase 'as well as' is parenthetical.

question_text: We are not surprised he was not elected; every one of his constituents _______ that he is unreliable.
explanation: 'Every one' is singular and takes the singular verb 'knows'.

question_text: Each of the candidates that came late _______ to complete _______.
explanation: 'Each' is singular, taking 'has' and 'this form'.

question_text: Either the chief or the leader of the farmers _______ to be held responsible for the revolt.
explanation: 'Either/or' follows the nearest subject. 'The leader' is singular, so 'is' is correct.

question_text: We must observe that most of the support by other states _______ only marginal returns.
explanation: The subject is 'most of the support' (singular, as 'support' is uncountable), so 'has yielded' is correct.

question_text: Only observers from the Ministry of Works _______ allowed into the conference room.
explanation: The subject 'observers' is plural, so 'are' is correct.

question_text: A panel set up to probe the organization's activities _______ yet to sit.
explanation: The subject is 'A panel' (singular), so 'is' is correct.

question_text: Every programming language and software package _______.
explanation: Subjects joined by 'and' but preceded by 'every' take a singular verb and singular pronoun: 'has its'.

question_text: Three quarters of the Physics class _______.
explanation: The subject 'Three quarters' is plural (referring to students), so 'improve' is correct.

question_text: A number of students _______.
explanation: 'A number of' takes a plural verb. 'Have' is correct.

question_text: Ahmed is one of the boys who always _______.
explanation: 'One of the boys who' takes a singular verb 'does' in this context, agreeing with 'one'.

question_text: A survey of opinions on how pupils feel about their teachers _______.
explanation: The subject 'A survey' is singular, so 'has been' is correct.

question_text: The principal and chairman of the occasion _______ arrived.
explanation: 'The principal and chairman of the occasion' refers to the same person (no second article 'the'), so it takes a singular verb 'has'.

question_text: One of the _______ that highlights the usefulness of thought suggest _______ selective marking of errors.
explanation: 'One of the' is followed by a plural noun ('schools'). The verb for 'that' agrees with the plural noun ('suggest').

question_text: All is crying because his mother was killed in a _______.
explanation: The standard phrase is 'road accident'.

question_text: Some of the food _______.
explanation: 'Food' is an uncountable noun, so it takes a singular verb 'is'.

question_text: When the teacher asked him to join the queue outside, he considered it _______.
explanation: An 'affront' is an action or remark that causes outrage or offense.

question_text: When he joined the staff of the school, he had various duties _______.
explanation: To be 'assigned' duties means to be given tasks.

question_text: After a long talk with the police, Baba confessed his guilt and so the other boys with whom he was accused were _______.
explanation: To be 'exonerated' means to be absolved of blame.

question_text: The vermin on his body _______ him look hideous.
explanation: 'Vermin' is an uncountable noun that takes a singular verb 'makes'.

question_text: The company was charged with _______ and breach of contract.
explanation: 'Negligence' is failure to take proper care, which fits the legal context.

question_text: The helpless _______ our sympathy.
explanation: 'The helpless' is a plural noun phrase referring to people, so it takes 'require'.

question_text: My brother got married to a woman with _______
explanation: 'Exquisite' means extremely beautiful and delicate.

question_text: How can we believe this witness when no one will _______ his story?
explanation: To 'corroborate' a story means to confirm or give support to it.

question_text: Moses, _______ is a car _______ now no longer impossible to manage these days.
explanation: The subject is 'Moses' (singular), so it takes the singular verb 'is'.

question_text: The police _______ that they say is _______ happy about the dwindling crime rate.
explanation: 'Police' is a plural noun taking 'say' and 'are'.

question_text: A range of options _______.
explanation: 'A range' is singular, so it takes 'is made'.

question_text: The trader _______ displayed to the public during the recently concluded elections.
explanation: 'Exhibited' is the formal verb for displaying items publicly.

question_text: The exercise will be easily accomplished by the team if members _______.
explanation: The correct phrasal verb is 'pool resources together'.

question_text: Sixty percent of the unskilled workers _______.
explanation: 'Sixty percent of' takes a plural verb 'were retained'.

question_text: Defects like in government's development plans _______.
explanation: The subject 'Defects' is plural, so it takes 'are'.

question_text: Either Ekate or you _______ to be blamed.
explanation: In an 'either/or' construction, the verb agrees with the nearest subject ('you' -> 'are').

question_text: The teacher with his wife _______ here.
explanation: The subject 'The teacher' is singular. 'With his wife' is parenthetical. 'Is' is correct.

question_text: He is one of those who _______ teaching in my school.
explanation: 'One of those who' takes a plural verb because 'who' refers to 'those' (plural). 'Are teaching' is correct.

question_text: The director, no less than his workers, _______ to blame.
explanation: The subject is 'The director' (singular). 'No less than his workers' is parenthetical. 'Is' is correct.

question_text: The fact that Olu was able to guess correctly some of the questions that were asked, made him _______.
explanation: 'Have an edge over' means to have an advantage over someone.

question_text: One of the vice _______ a president acts in an interim capacity.
explanation: 'One of the' is followed by a plural noun 'presidents'.

question_text: You should read all the _______ carefully before you decide where to go on holiday.
explanation: A 'brochure' is a magazine or booklet containing pictures and information about a product or service.

question_text: The Emir and conqueror of the enemy territories _______ next week.
explanation: 'The Emir and conqueror' refers to the same person, so the verb is singular 'arrives'.

question_text: Where _______ does these go?
explanation: 'These' is plural, so it takes 'do'. 'Where do these go?' is correct.

question_text: Our lives _______ a resource base.
explanation: 'Our lives' is plural, so it takes 'are'.

question_text: A sterile range _______ mountains, broken at intervals by deep ravines.
explanation: 'A sterile range' is singular, so it takes 'encloses'.

question_text: The whole of optimists of regaining his freedom because the accused is to _______ confront a challenge.
explanation: The context requires a passive verb 'has been arrested'.

question_text: Three-quarters of the members _______ during the meeting.
explanation: 'Three-quarters of the members' takes a plural verb 'were present'.

question_text: Two young boys have been caught with parts of the stolen machines, but _______ of them has been released.
explanation: 'Neither' means not one nor the other, fitting the context of them not being released.

question_text: The rebels will soon _______ control of the city.
explanation: To 'assume control' means to take control.

question_text: Al is honest and quiet as a schoolboy, but too much drinking has changed his _______ and temperament.
explanation: 'Character' fits the context of personality traits.

question_text: The doctor's _______ from the hospital was a loss to the whole hospital.
explanation: 'Dismissal' is the noun form meaning the act of being removed from a job.

question_text: Neither John nor his parents _______ at home.
explanation: In a 'neither/nor' construction, the verb agrees with the nearest subject 'parents' (plural).

question_text: At the last minute, the goal-keeper saved the ball from going into the net.
option_c: saved the ball from going into the net
explanation: To 'save' a ball means to stop it from going into the goal.

question_text: He was short of cash so he _______ down the hill with the engine switched off.
explanation: To 'coast' means to move easily without power.

question_text: The students were all _______ tired to go on with the examination.
explanation: 'Too tired to' is the correct structure.

question_text: The new students were __________ than the old ones.
explanation: The comparative of 'good' is 'better'.

question_text: The reporter said that the Honourable Speaker _______ impeached.
explanation: In reported speech, 'may have been' changes to 'might have been'.

question_text: It is impossible to say whether _______ Ola and her sister will be offered jobs by the firm.
explanation: 'Whether either' is the correct structure for a choice between two.

question_text: The three-quarters of the earth's surface _______ covered by water.
explanation: 'Three-quarters of the earth's surface' is a singular measurement, taking 'is'.

question_text: The Governor has _______ to the people on many occasions.
explanation: The past tense of 'broadcast' can be 'broadcast'.

question_text: The _______ a historic review of the history of the country has marked the beginning of a new life for the entire cabinet.
explanation: 'History' is the noun.

question_text: The old man was rushed to hospital when his blood pressure dropped to a _______ dangerous low level.
explanation: The adverb 'dangerously' modifies the adjective 'low'.

question_text: The brave hunter killed _______.
explanation: The correct adjective order is size, color, participle.

question_text: His father hardly mentions the news because he goes about with _______.
explanation: 'A portable radio' is the correct phrase.

question_text: The scholar examined _______.
explanation: The compound adjective 'part-analysis' is correct.

question_text: The litigants finally opted _______.
explanation: The correct phrase is 'opted for an out-of-court settlement'.

question_text: His mother always reprimands him for being a _______.
explanation: 'Voracious' reader of cheap novels means an eager reader.
